coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies

coverage.category: 32. Telecom equipment distributors and SIM sellers (ARCT order 580/01 of 2025; SIM registration 2026)
coverage.found: ARCT order 580/01: distributors need ARCT authorisation, national register of approved products, fines up to BIF 5M plus confiscation. SIM re-registration began mid-June 2026 (in person with ID; no formal agent-registration duty stated; operators keep data 5 years).

ARCA ran field checks in 2017, 2018, 2022, 2023 and Feb-May 2024 and found most operators ignorant of the law. Sanctions and proof-of-cover form not found.

coverage.found: Farmers register through an approved MFI, pay a 40% share, and redeem vouchers at suppliers who are refunded by the ministry. BRIDEP (AfDB/IFAD, USD 323.75M, 2024-2029) is procuring digitisation of the scheme and geolocation of 120,000 households. The state is the buyer.

coverage.category: 36. Customs brokers and transit agents (OBR)
coverage.found: Only old SYDONIA++ material (2006, 2008, 2016). Current accreditation list and rules not found; new GUE web platform since Feb 2026.

coverage.category: 37. Insurance brokers and general agents (ARCA)
coverage.found: ARCA publishes lists of approved brokerage companies and professional-card holders; the brokers' association is IBAB. Conditions and reporting duties not found.

coverage.category: 38. Artisanal mining comptoirs and gold exporters (OBM)
coverage.found: OBM labels mineral bags before export; exporters must surrender forex to BRB; 2013 orders set comptoir contributions. EITI status and current comptoir rules not found.

coverage.found: Water Code (Law 1/02 of 26 Mar 2012, 158 articles) has a 'préleveur-payeur' principle. A 2024 decree sets protection perimeters for drinking-water intakes. I did not find the licence or abstraction-permit procedure, a driller register or the issuing agency. Law text not opened.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: AHAMR (rural water agency, set up 2015) hands water points to user associations and caretaker groups. Tariff and committee statutes not found. AREEN licenses and regulates operators but mainly regulates REGIDESO. Donor-funded and NGO-run, with no private software buyer identified.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Strong signal. A Saudi bilateral domestic-worker recruitment agreement was signed on 3 Oct 2021, and the Senate has examined a ratification bill. The Ministry of Public Service suspended all private employment agencies on 26 Jan 2021 'until further notice' after trafficking cases. The accord provides a guarantee fund funded by the agency associations. Agency licensing conditions, current status and list of agencies were not found. Candidate recorded as unverified.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: The NGO and ASBL framework is restrictive (AFD call notes national recognition is required). No concrete current annual-report text found beyond K04. Nothing new beyond K04.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers

result.reason: Duty is real: Code des assurances (loi 1/02 of 2014, art. 277-287, revised 2020) makes liability cover for fire/explosion compulsory for shops of at least 200 m2, bars/restaurants of at least 250 m2, and hotels of at least 15 guests (ARCA bulletin N°2). ARCA checked in 2017, 2018, 2022 and 2023, plus campaigns with communes in 2024. Compliance is very low: at the Jabe market fire in June 2026 only about 3 of roughly 100 traders were insured. No local tracker software found, and no Burundi e-certificate system (SNECA is the DRC's ARCA). Weak case: it is one annual policy, sanctions are not detailed, the premises count was not found, and willingness to pay is low. Also unverified: whether 2020 revisions changed the thresholds.

BRB Regulation 003/2024 (30 July 2024, commercial agents in banking and payment services) is real. A 2026 BRB regulation on BurundiPay (03/2026) cites it, so it appears still in force. I could not read the text. The regalert fetch returned 429, and the only sources are auto-generated summaries. Whether individual agents or only the payment institutions file the periodic compliance reports is unknown. The duty most likely sits with the operators and banks, which supervise their own agents. I found no agent-compliance software or sub-agent tier data. The buyer is probably the operator, and small agents have low willingness to pay. The market is large: Lumicash had about 16.8k agents by 2018. Weak fit for a solo founder.

result.competitor: ITSCI traceability (3T) and SGS pre-shipment verification; no dedicated comptoir software found
result.market: Unknown number of licensed comptoirs; ITSCI names two 3T exporters (BME, RMR)
result.reason: Two searches found no current source on OBM bag labelling, BRB forex surrender rules for 2026, or the number of licensed gold comptoirs. They only gave dated context. A 2016 BRB announcement covered repatriating export forex. A 2016 decree gave OBM its monitoring and revenue-collection role. ITSCI names two 3T exporters, BME and RMR. The buyer group is probably a handful of firms, so this is a very small market. Buyers are hard to reach, the sector is informal, and ITSCI, SGS and state traceability processes already cover part of the job. Weak fit for a solo founder; I'd score it 2. Not checked: current OBM rules, the comptoir register, and a software competitor search.

decisions.reason: Shops, bars and hotels are small firms with a mandatory recurring insurance duty; verifiers can test willingness to pay.
Small agents and super-agents carry a recurring BRB approval and reporting duty; in scope, operator coverage is for verifiers.
Comptoirs and exporters are a different buyer and duty from K05 (cooperative site registers); new candidate related to K05.
Small COOPECs and microfinance institutions have a recurring BRB reporting and audit duty; cooperatives are in scope and no known idea covers it.
Phone shops and importers must hold ARCT authorisation and sell only type-approved devices; a new buyer and duty.
Small guard companies have a recurring permit and social-security file duty; in scope and not a known idea.
Agro-dealers and MFIs face a recurring voucher redemption and refund process; a new buyer and duty. Whether it is a state system is for verifiers.
Private vet clinics and vet pharmacies have a licensing and stock register duty. K09 covers livestock traders, so this is a different buyer and duty.
Small brokers and agents have a professional-card and reporting duty to ARCA, which puts it in scope.
Households as employers have a mandatory INSS registration and monthly declaration duty, which is in scope; no known idea covers it.
Same buyers and the same OBR EBMS e-invoicing duty as K06, K03 and K08; no concrete new evidence is cited.
Same pharmacies and importers and the same ABREMA import permit dossier duty as K02.
Same coffee washing stations and exporters and the same EUDR traceability duty as K01.
Recruitment agencies are small firms with a licensing and placement duty under the 2021 Saudi agreement; no known idea covers it.
Private drillers and commercial water users have a permit and fee duty under the Water Code; a new buyer and duty, and the unconfirmed procedure is for verifiers.
